entries.title: Solar Wind Stream Past a Magnetized Earth
entries.description: A glowing yellow “solar wind” of moving particle spheres streams from a bright solar disc toward a blue Earth sphere with a transparent magnetic field bubble, where particles are deflected into curved trajectories, trapped in donut-shaped radiation belts, or collide with the atmosphere and trigger aurora-like curtains of shifting color near the poles.

entries.title: Solar Wind Pressure Sculpting a Comet Tail
entries.description: A dusty comet nucleus ball orbits a pale Sun while a constant solar wind of small particles and arrows pushes out two semi-transparent tails (ion tail glowing blue and dust tail white) that always stream away from the Sun, with particles detaching from the comet and being swept into long, curved trails.

entries.title: Magnetic Field Lines and Solar Wind Reconnection
entries.description: A section of the Sun emits arched, semi-transparent magnetic field tubes while a flow of charged solar wind particles approaches Earth’s magnetosphere; field lines bend, merge, and reconnect, flinging particle clouds along newly formed field lines that pulse and change color where reconnection occurs.

entries.title: Solar Wind Eroding a Planet Without a Magnetic Field
entries.description: A rocky, atmosphere-wrapped planet without a magnetosphere is bombarded by a dense stream of solar wind particles that strip away atmospheric particles, which detach and stream off into space in colored trails, while a side meter tracks atmospheric loss over time.

entries.title: Solar Wind Driving a Solar Sail Spacecraft
entries.description: A thin, reflective, square solar sail plane orbits a bright Sun while a stream of solar wind particles collides with its surface, transferring momentum and slowly changing the spacecraft’s trajectory, with vector arrows and trails showing changing velocity and adjustable sail tilt.

entries.title: Heliosphere Bubble in the Interstellar Medium
entries.description: A glowing yellow Sun at the center emits expanding solar wind particles that form a large transparent bubble (the heliosphere) pushing against a contrasting flow of interstellar medium particles, with a boundary surface that ripples, compresses, and shifts as solar wind intensity is increased or decreased by a control slider.

entries.title: Solar Wind and Polar Aurora Curtains
entries.description: A tilted Earth with visible magnetic field lines is bathed in a steady solar wind; some charged particles spiral along field lines and collide with the polar upper atmosphere, spawning vertical, semi-transparent aurora sheets that glow green, purple, and red and dance, fade, and reform with particle impacts.

entries.title: Coronal Mass Ejection Blasting Past Planets
entries.description: A large, bright CME cloud erupts from the Sun as an expanding shell of glowing particles and semi-transparent plasma, engulfing and compressing the magnetospheres of several orbiting planets, causing their magnetic bubbles to squash, oscillate, and release bursts of trapped particles trailing behind.

entries.title: Solar Wind Charging and Deflecting a Lunar Dust Cloud
entries.description: A gray Moon sphere with a low, weak exosphere is bombarded by solar wind particles that charge dust grains on the surface; charged dust spheres detach, float, and hover above the surface, forming a tenuous dust halo that shifts toward or away from the Sun depending on wind direction and strength.

entries.title: Solar Wind Interaction with a Planetary Ring System
entries.description: A ringed planet sits in a mild solar wind stream, with ring particles represented by small spheres; solar wind gradually charges and perturbs the outer rings, causing some particles to spiral inward or outward, clump, collide, and scatter, leaving bright trails where they cross the planetary magnetic field.

entries.title: Solar Wind as an Interplanetary Weather System
entries.description: A top-down view of the inner solar system shows the Sun at the center and several planets orbiting, while semi-transparent “gusts” and streams of solar wind sweep outward as rotating spiral arms, occasionally intensifying into bright patches that slam into planets and temporarily brighten their magnetospheres.

entries.title: Solar Wind Deflection by an Artificial Magnetic Shield
entries.description: A small colony habitat near Mars is protected by a simulated artificial magnetic dipole field; solar wind particles approach and either get deflected around the field, spiral along artificial field lines, or hit unshielded parts of the habitat, with color-coded impact counts displayed as dynamic labels.

entries.title: Solar Wind Sculpting a Planetary Magnetotail
entries.description: A magnetic planet sits in a continuous solar wind stream, with its dayside field compressed and a long magnetotail stretching away; particle tracers show solar wind entering the tail, reconnecting, and accelerating back toward the planet or out into space, with the tail shape flexing and waving over time.

entries.title: Solar Wind Ionization of a Cometary Atmosphere

entries.title: Solar Wind Pressure on a Space Station Radiator System
entries.description: A rotating space station with extended thin radiator panels experiences a variable solar wind; as wind direction and intensity sliders change, the panels flex, twist, or fold automatically to reduce stress, with vectors indicating pressure on each panel and trails showing the station’s slow orbital drift.
